thread:
Elaine: Quick question — customers are confused about how API requests from service accounts get attributed in the console (billing vs policy logs).
Mike: Which mismatch are you seeing?
Elaine: Example: SA key created in project-alpha mints tokens that `act_as` project-beta. Billing shows project-alpha, policy/audit shows project-beta. Users ask 'who gets charged' and it's unclear.
TJ: We purposely separated origin vs effective attribution. Proposal: add explicit fields `x-rd-origin-project` and `x-rd-effective-project` in the request envelope so downstream services can decide.
Sasha: +1. For UI, we should surface both but make clear what drives quota consumption (org vs project).
Mike: How would this affect routing policies? Current path uses origin_project for routing affinity and quota lookup. Changing that could break lots of heuristics.
TJ: Routing stays as-is by default. Engine should evaluate: if token carries `effective_project` (explicit override via impersonation), use that for quota and billing only when flag `use_effective_for_quota=true`. Otherwise fallback to origin.
Elaine: UX idea: Request header hover in console: "Attributed to: project-beta (origin key: project-alpha)" with a small tooltip explaining rules. :information_source:
Sasha: One more: service accounts minted by org-level service identity may need org-level quota. Need to support three levels: origin_project, effective_project, effective_org.
Mike: Telemetry ask: add metric `auth.attribution.change` with tags: origin, effective, org, quota_source, mismatch=true/false. That will help us see how often customers hit ambiguous attribution.
TJ: Also add an `attribution_reason` enum: CREATED_KEY, IMPERSONATION, ORG_BINDING, FALLBACK. Put it in logs and the new headers so we can trace.
Elaine: Security concern: exposing `origin_project` broadly might leak internal mapping for cross-org service accounts. We should gate visibility in console behind RBAC (owners + security).
Sasha: Agree. Support logs should redact origin unless request is flagged for investigation.
Mike: Operational note: we need a migration plan. Phase 1: auth-proxy emits new headers and metrics (canary 5%). Phase 2: console shows both labels for customers who opt-in. Phase 3: admin toggle to flip default quota attribution to `effective` for customers who want that behavior.
deploy-bot: auth-proxy v3.1 canary rollout scheduled tonight 02:00 UTC, 5% traffic.
TJ: Implementation detail: headers `x-rd-origin-project` and `x-rd-attribution-reason` are signed by auth-proxy to prevent tampering. Also we should canonicalize project ids to `org/project` form.
Elaine: For quotas, rule proposal (in order): 1) If token has org-binding -> charge org. 2) Else if `use_effective_for_quota` set AND effective_project present -> charge effective. 3) Else charge origin_project. Documented and visible in console.
Sasha: We must add dedicated-customer override: some enterprise accounts want to force billing to their org regardless. Add a per-customer policy flag.
Mike: I'll check quota-engine edgecases for burst/batching where attribution changes mid-request. Might need atomic attribution snapshot per RPC.
Elaine: Thanks. @Sasha can you write an RFC with the header schema + UI mockups?
Sasha: Will do, PR tonight.
Mike: Follow-up: I'll create an ops-runbook for canary rollback criteria (increase in `auth.attribution.change` or spike in 5xx from quota checks).
Elaine: Awesome. Short next steps: Sasha RFC, TJ implement header signing, Mike ops checks, Iiter on UI copy.
Mike: noted.
Elaine: closing — will sync in eng-platform sync on Friday. :white_check_mark:
